headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap make prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts plausible by default; xonsh’s isolated environment only partially reduces blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP and shared filesystem state, while xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Goose ingests xonsh-produced files or logs as trusted input. xonsh’s isolated environment lowers but does not remove the risk.
conditions: IF Goose reads xonsh-written files or stdout as instructions, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Require manual review before Goose acts on xonsh output.
Prefix all machine-generated files with provenance metadata.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing to the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and filesystem contents, and Goose has broad network egress plus handles model-provider and extension tokens. If they share a workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files; Goose can also transmit them outward. xonsh’s isolated environment helps, but the shared filesystem path keeps leakage plausible.
conditions: IF the agents share a directory containing secrets or credentials, leakage is possible.
IF Goose is pointed at sensitive files, its network egress can exfiltrate them.
mitigations: Use separate least-privilege directories.
Remove secrets from shared workspaces.
Block outbound network for Goose during sensitive tasks.
Mount read-only inputs for xonsh.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose and xonsh both have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning. Goose also modifies git state and supports multiple instances via shared filesystem, while xonsh does not support multiple instances. Concurrent writes to the same repo or cwd can corrupt files or git state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF both write the same file or branch without locks, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign one writer per repository.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Use separate branches per agent.
Run one agent read-only during the other’s write phase.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce tool-using outputs and xonsh can execute shell commands, so Goose’s output may become xonsh input with little verification. That makes mistaken commands or bad facts cascade into real actions. xonsh’s isolated environment is helpful, but not enough to guarantee review before execution.
conditions: IF xonsh executes Goose-generated commands without review, errors propagate to the shell.
IF Goose emits incorrect file paths or commands, xonsh may act on them directly.
mitigations: Require human approval before execution.
Insert a validation step between agents.
Log and diff proposed commands before running them.
Restrict xonsh to dry-run mode for generated commands.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. The main compliance concern is operational: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, while xonsh touches environment variables and filesystem contents. No explicit residency or HIPAA/GDPR mismatch is documented, so only a small documented-gap risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, policy review is required.
IF Goose extensions send data to external providers, local retention assumptions may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review extension destinations before use.
Disable unnecessary extensions.
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent.
